t2798.bio: Ibn Ḥajar records Shuʿayb ibn Abī Ḥamza al-Umawī, whose father's name was Dīnār, Abū Bishr al-Ḥimṣī, trustworthy and devout; Ibn Maʿīn said he was one of the most reliable in al-Zuhrī; of the seventh generation, died 162 or after.
as: one of the most reliable of people in al-Zuhrī
Yaḥyā ibn Maʿīn, quoted by al-Mizzī
ثقة، وكان عسرا في حديثه، وكان سماعه من الزهري مع الولاة
Reliable. He was difficult to obtain hadith from, and he heard from al-Zuhrī in the company of governors.
Aḥmad ibn Ḥanbal, quoted by al-Mizzī
رأيت كتب شعيب بن أبي حمزة فرأيت كتبا مضبوطة مقيدة
I saw Shuʿayb’s books and found them precisely written and annotated.
Aḥmad ibn Ḥanbal, quoted by al-Mizzī
قلت: أين هو من يونس؟ قال: فوقه. قلت: فأين هو من الزبيدي؟ قال: مثله.
Asked how Shuʿayb ranked, Aḥmad placed him above Yūnus and on a par with al-Zubaydī.
Aḥmad ibn Ḥanbal, quoted by al-Mizzī
Yaḥyā ibn Maʿīn, quoted by al-Mizzī
ثقة مثل يونس وعقيل يعني في الزهري.
Trustworthy, like Yūnus and ʿUqayl in transmitting from al-Zuhrī.
Yaḥyā ibn Maʿīn, quoted by al-Mizzī
شعيب من اثبت الناس في الزهري كان كاتبا.
Shuʿayb was among the most dependable transmitters from al-Zuhrī. He was a scribe.
Yaʿqūb ibn Shaybah, quoted by al-Mizzī
Abū Ḥātim al-Rāzī, quoted by al-Mizzī
علي بن عباس, quoted by al-Mizzī
وكان ضنينا بالحديث، كان يعدنا المجلس فنقيم نقتضيه إياه، فإذا فعل، فإنما كتابه بيده ما يأخذه أحد، وكان من صنف آخر في العبادة
He was sparing with his hadith. We would keep asking him to honor the appointment he had promised. When he did, he retained his book in his hand. He was in a class of his own in worship.
He was reluctant to transmit hadith.

t4345.bio: Ibn Ḥajar records ʿUbayd Allāh ibn Mūsā ibn Bādhām al-ʿAbsī al-Kūfī, Abū Muḥammad, as trustworthy and a Shiʿi, of the ninth generation; Abū Ḥātim said he was more firmly established in Isrāʾīl than Abū Nuʿaym and deemed too young in Sufyān al-Thawrī. He died in the year 13 (hundreds omitted), according to the correct view.
as: كان أثبت في إسرائيل من أبي نعيم واستصغر في سفيان الثوري
He was more firmly established in [the transmission of] Isrāʾīl than Abū Nuʿaym, and he was deemed too young in [the transmission of] Sufyān al-Thawrī.
Aḥmad ibn Ḥanbal, quoted by al-Mizzī
كان صاحب تخليط وحدث بأحاديث سوء أخرج تلك البلايا فحدث بها
He confused reports and transmitted bad hadiths. He brought out those objectionable reports and narrated them.
Aḥmad ibn Ḥanbal, quoted by al-Mizzī
لم يكن مثله، كان أستر منه، وأما هو فأخرج تلك الأحاديث الردية
Ibn Fuḍayl was more discreet, while ʿUbayd Allāh produced those bad hadiths.
Yaḥyā ibn Maʿīn, quoted by al-Mizzī
Yaḥyā ibn Maʿīn, quoted by al-Mizzī
Write from him, as we wrote from him.
Abū Ḥātim al-Rāzī, quoted by al-Mizzī
صدوق، ثقة، حسن الحديث، وأبو نعيم أتقن منه، وعبيد الله أثبتهم في إسرائيل، كان إسرائيل يأتيه فيقرأ عليه القرآن
Truthful and reliable, with good hadith. Abū Nuʿaym was more exact, while ʿUbayd Allāh was the most precise of them on Isrāʾīl, who used to visit him and recite the Qurʾān to him.
ثقة، وكان عالما بالقرآن، رأسا فيه
Trustworthy, a scholar of the Qurʾān and a leader in it.
He was an ardent Shīʿī, and his hadith was admissible.
ما رأيته رافعا رأسه وما رئي ضاحكا قط
I never saw him raise his head, and he was never seen laughing.
وكان ثقة صدوقا إن شاء الله كثير الحديث حسن الهيئة
He was trustworthy and truthful, God willing, transmitted many hadiths, and had a good appearance.
وكان يتشيع ويروي أحاديث في التشيع منكرة فضعف بذلك عند كثير من الناس
He had Shīʿī leanings and narrated objectionable hadiths on Shīʿism, so many people judged him weak.
He was devoted to the Qurʾān.

t7748.bio: Ibn Ḥajar records Yazīd ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Abī Mālik al-Hamadānī al-Dimashqī the judge, truthful but may err, of the fourth generation. He died in 130 AH or after, over seventy years old.

t8042.bio: Ibn Ḥajar records Abū Ḥarb ibn Abī al-Aswad al-Daylī al-Baṣrī as trustworthy, of the third generation, who died in 108; his name is given as Miḥjan or ʿAṭāʾ.

t8158.bio: Ibn Ḥajar records Abū Shurayḥ al-Khuzāʿī al-Kaʿbī as a Companion who settled in Medina and died in 68 AH, with disagreement over his name.

t8253.bio: Ibn Ḥajar says Abū ʿAṭiyya al-Wādiʿī al-Hamadānī, whose name is given with several possibilities, is trustworthy, of the second generation, and died around the year seventy.

tinnisi.bio: A transmitter of Mālik’s Muwaṭṭaʾ. Ibn Ḥajar singles out his precision in transmitting that work.
as: ثقة متقن من أثبت الناس في الموطأ
Trustworthy and precise, among the firmest transmitters of the Muwaṭṭaʾ.
وعبد الله بن يوسف صدوق، لا بأس به، والبخاري مع شدة استقصائه، اعتمد عليه في مالك وغيره، وسمع منه"الموطأ"، وله أحاديث صالحة، وهو خير فاضل.

ʿAbd Allāh ibn Yūsuf was truthful and acceptable. Al-Bukhārī relied on him for Mālik and others despite his exacting standards and heard the Muwaṭṭaʾ from him. He had sound reports and was good and virtuous.
Yaḥyā ibn Maʿīn, quoted by al-Mizzī
أثبت الناس في "الموطإ"عبد الله بن مسلمة القعنبي، وعبد الله بن يوسف التنيسي بعده.
The firmest transmitter of the Muwaṭṭaʾ was ʿAbd Allāh ibn Maslamah al-Qaʿnabī, followed by ʿAbd Allāh ibn Yūsuf al-Tinnīsī.
Yaḥyā ibn Maʿīn, quoted by al-Mizzī
ما بقي علي أديم الأرض أحد أوثق في "الموطأ"، من عبد الله بن يوسف التنيسي.
No one alive was more reliable for the Muwaṭṭaʾ than ʿAbd Allāh ibn Yūsuf al-Tinnīsī.
وأبو حاتم محمد بن إدريس الرازي, quoted by al-Mizzī
هو أتقن من مروان الطاطري، وهو ثقة.
He was more exact than Marwān al-Ṭāṭarī, and he was trustworthy.
He was among the firmest Syrian transmitters.
عبد الله بن يوسف الثقة المقنع.
ʿAbd Allāh ibn Yūsuf was trustworthy and satisfactory.
متى سمع من مالك؟ ، ومن رآه عند مالك؟
When did he hear from Mālik, and who saw him with Mālik?
وكان ثقة حسن الحديث، وعنده"الموطأ"عن مالك، وعنده مسائل سوي"الموطأ"عن مالك.
He was trustworthy, with good hadith. He had the Muwaṭṭaʾ and other questions from Mālik.
